description: Hand-written validator conformance cases. Go (internal/contracts) and Python (tradestocker_research.contracts) must both give exactly the expected answer for every case. expect is "valid", {"code": MALFORMED_JSON | SCHEMA_ERROR}, or {"keyword", "path"} of the first violation. documents maps a document name to its JSON text; contracts: true loads the real contracts/events/v1 documents instead. Depth counts from 0 at the top value; a value deeper than 64 is refused. String rules apply in order minLength, maxLength, pattern, format.

042: top-level alternation is refused
cases.rationale: Review 042 ran an earlier engine that used each language's regex library: Go matched part of the string and Python the whole, and each accepted syntax the other refused. Both now use the dialect's own grammar and automaton (pattern.go). ^a|b$ accepted "ax" in Go but not in Python.

cases.name: 042: nested repetition compiles
cases.rationale: Review 042 found that both regex libraries accepted ^(a+)+$, which backtracks exponentially in Python (compile-only probe, never matched). The dialect's automaton has no backtracking, so nested repetition is now accepted and matched in linear time.

cases.name: 042: nested repetition refuses a near miss without backtracking
cases.rationale: Review 042 found that both regex libraries accepted ^(a+)+$, which backtracks exponentially in Python (compile-only probe, never matched). The dialect's automaton has no backtracking, so nested repetition is now accepted and matched in linear time.

cases.name: depth: 64-document chain compiled leaf first
cases.rationale: Review 042: a 600-document reference chain passed in Go and exhausted Python's recursion. Review 044/045: cached subtrees bypassed the depth limit when documents compiled leaf first. Depth is now tracked with each cached subtree's height, the same in both languages and in any compile order.
